mathematical_assessments.reason: The two-normalization transition formula is computed in the Hermitian model. Applying Shimizu to g T_ell_j g^-1, rather than assuming the coordinate transition belongs to the group, correctly gives |c|^2 ell_i ell_j >= 1. Rank-one transverse strip bounds and rank-two height bounds give disjoint larger extended-region closures, including finite ideal peaks; the log-rho dual norm gives the asserted 2 log(2) separation for smaller closures. Dirichlet inequalities bound all horizontal coordinates outside an individual extended region. With center o in C, every Dirichlet limit-vertex ray lies in D intersect C and crosses the corresponding separated region boundary, except possibly one containing o. Compactness of the truncated D intersect C therefore gives finitely many actual Dirichlet limit vertices, not merely finitely many cusp orbits. Full-D coordinate bounds exclude accumulation at removed parabolic vertices, proving the compactified truncation assertion.

The actual holomorphic covering pullbacks, component-orbit stabilizer invariance and countable component assembly give a measurable invariant coefficient with the supplied 0<=kappa<1, without assuming null limit-set area or simply connected components. The invariant-Beltrami supplier proves discrete faithful Mobius conjugacy and the independently reviewed GF-preservation chain gives the actual volume definition. Equal coefficients cancel in local quotient sheets, proving exact biholomorphisms I_j fbar_j = m_j. Parabolic stabilizer, rank, primitive generator and supplied end-label claims follow from exact conjugacy and exact marking equality. Empty component collection and conformal markings give the zero coefficient and normalized identity.

Discrete second-countable matrix groups give only countably many parabolic points. At each conical point the normalized isometries have a compact-frame subsequential limit. A fixed discontinuity disc supplies a fixed Euclidean subdisc away from zero in the normalized images. Inversion produces genuine holes of area at least a constant times Y_n^-2 inside balls of radius C/Y_n, so the conical point is not a density-one point. Smooth conformal coordinate changes preserve density one. The actual density theorem and conical-or-bounded-parabolic criterion then prove area zero; the proof does not infer area zero from empty interior or apply it to a lattice limit sphere.

Normalized QC compactness gives the uniform quasidisk interior-ball estimate. Packing proves finitely many component closures at each boundary point and a null family of component diameters. Conical boundary collapse plus that null family gives stabilizer limit points; finite incidence plus a power of the ambient parabolic handles parabolic boundary points, proving the full component-stabilizer limit set and nonelementarity. Lifted marked homotopies yield exactly equivariant biholomorphic component lifts. Dense stabilizer loxodromic endpoints force their correction maps to fix boundaries pointwise. The round-circle extension is proved by global L2 energy, ACL on almost all closed chords and weak integration by parts. Uniform quasidisk charts give a common QC bound for disjoint-support finite compositions; normalized compactness makes the prescribed infinite gluing a genuine global QC map. Null-area transport then makes the final global correction conformal almost everywhere and hence Mobius. The empty discontinuity-domain case uses a proved finite-volume-to-finite-Haar frame measure and unimodularity bridge, followed by the actual full L2 contraction-rigidity supplier. The common triple is correctly required to lie on the limit set for the identity conclusion.
